title: Best Poster Designers (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire a poster designer for events, films, shops or campaigns: what to include, print files, how to brief it, price factors and red flags.
intro: A poster has to catch attention from across a room or street and deliver its message in seconds. It is used for events, films, shops, campaigns and decoration. Posters go wrong when there is too much text, the file is not set up for the printer's size, or images are used without a license. This guide helps you order a poster that is striking, readable and ready to print.

faq.q: Which size should my poster be?
faq.a: Common sizes include A3, A2, A1 and US poster sizes such as 18 by 24 inches. Choose the size based on where it will hang and how far away people will be, and confirm it with your printer.

faq.q: What resolution does a poster need?
faq.a: High enough for its print size. Large posters need large, high-resolution images. Ask the designer to prepare the file at the printer's required size and resolution.

faq.q: Can I also use the design online?
faq.a: Yes. Ask for digital versions for social media and your website in the same order, since they need different sizes and compression.

faq.q: How much text should a poster have?
faq.a: As little as possible: a strong headline, the key details such as date and place, and one action. People read posters from a distance and in passing.
Confirm you may use the design for printing and promotion. If the poster uses illustrations or photos, check their licenses too.
